newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Prices firm at Napier and Dunedin wool sales.
newsitem.headline: Prices firm at Napier and Dunedin wool sales.

text.p: With the exception of merino wools, prices generally improved slightly at sales in Napier and Dunedin on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.
The market indicator rose one cent to NZ$4.60. The fine segment indicator fell two cents to $8.08, medium segment rose four to $4.83, and the strong segment rose one to $4.25.

Merino fleece ranged from 10 percent cheaper for 18 micron to slightly dearer for 17 micron. Halfbred fleece was generally unchanged, as was second shear and bulky skirtings while second shear bellies and pieces were 10-15 percent dearer.
Main interest came from China, Western Europe, local mills and Japan with support from Turkey, Australia and Nepal.
Some 22 percent of the 3,467 tonnes on offer was passed in.
The sale comprised 37 percent crossbred fleece, 18 percent merino, 11 percent halfbred fleece, 12 percent second shear and miscellaneous other wools.
The next sale will be in Christchurch on October 17.
